processing_steps.atmosphere: argon gas injected into the melt chamber, maintaining a 600-millibar pressure; manganese added after Ar injection
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 2.5 kg ingot of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting.
The cast ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h prior to hot forging.
Hot forged between 1200 °C–900 °C ensuring more than 60% deformation with intermediate heating, then cooled by water quenching.

The forged material is solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and water quenched to retain maximum austenite phase. This is the defining step of the MAF-0 (0 pass) state; the sample is not subsequently multiaxially forged (0 MAF pass).

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenite-based (majority austenite) low-density steel; coarse-grained, strongly textured, essentially strain-free coarse equiaxed grains after solutionizing and water quenching. Face-centred-cubic (FCC) austenite reflections dominate the XRD pattern with minor κ-carbide reflections.
structures.number_of_phases: 1 (majority austenite, γ; minor κ-carbide reflections also present)

microstructure_list.region: analysed area for XRD/EBSD (central plate of the MAFed block, Fig. 3a)

phases_present.texture: strong texture; the [101] direction of a significant number of grains is parallel to the pressing direction

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: relatively wide; the MAF-0 area-fraction–grain-size curve is the broadest with the highest area fraction (just above 0.3) near 30–40 μm
grain_structure.texture: strongly textured; the normal direction of a significant amount of grains is parallel to [101] (pressing direction); solutionized sample shows the (111) peak as most intense (preferred orientation)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: miniature round tensile specimen, gauge length 16 mm, overall length 26.5 mm, gauge diameter Ø4 mm, shoulder diameter Ø7.2 mm, fillet radius R1 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Two round tensile samples taken from the chosen MAF pass to confirm reliability; plastic-gauge-length increase measured physically after fracture.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of MAF-0 (grey): starts near 400 MPa, work-hardens continuously to a broad maximum between 600 and 800 MPa at strain ≈0.6–0.7, then softens to roughly 550 MPa, ending near strain 0.75 — the most ductile condition.

strain_hardening_rate.note: highest amount of work hardening, calculated for the solutionized material (difference between UTS and YS)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scan speed 2° per minute, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 40°–120°; samples electro-polished before measurement; instrumental broadening (from standard silicon data) subtracted
characterization_methods.purpose: phase identification, crystallite size and lattice microstrain determination (Williamson–Hall) and dislocation-density estimation
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dominant FCC austenite reflections γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) plus weaker κ(220) carbide; γ(111) near 50° 2θ is the most intense peak in MAF-0. Average crystallite size 61 nm, average microstrain 3.66 × 10^-3, dislocation density 0.79 × 10^15 m^-2 (Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: grain boundaries located with misorientation angles greater than 15 degrees (equivalent grain size method); image quality maps with high/low angle boundary fractions and inverse pole figure (IPF) maps of the normal/pressing direction
characterization_methods.purpose: determine grain boundary character, texture and average grain size
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-0 shows high angle boundary fraction 0.62 (low angle boundary fraction 0.367/0.29–0.37); coarse equiaxed grains; IPF map shows strong texture with a significant number of grains having [101] parallel to the pressing direction; average grain size 50 μm.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: KAM map with unique colour map (Min 0 / Max 5), 60 μm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: assess local misorientation / stored plastic deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-0 reports an average KAM value of 0.34°, indicating minimal plastic deformation persisting even after solution annealing (uniformly low-misorientation/dark blue map).

characterization_methods.purpose: verify the measured average grain size
characterization_methods.key_findings: The solutionized and quenched material has grains of average size 50 μm (also verified from optical microstructure).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1, room temperature; miniature round tensile specimen (gauge length 16 mm, gauge Ø4 mm)
characterization_methods.purpose: measure tensile strength and elongation of each MAF condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-0 yield strength 380 MPa; UTS 762 MPa; total elongation 75%; uniform elongation 63%; work hardening 392 MPa.

characterization_methods.technique: Combustion infrared detection analysis (carbon) and wet chemical analysis (other elements)
characterization_methods.purpose: determine actual alloy composition after solutionization
characterization_methods.key_findings: Actual composition after solutionization is Fe-30.6Mn-9.1Al-0.79 C.

computational_details.simulation_method: 3-D finite element simulation of multiaxial forging (MAF) using the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) implemented via a VUMAT user subroutine; explicit dynamic technique
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model incorporating dislocation density and grain size effects (Eqs. 6–8); model parameters from Table 4
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 3-D model dimensions 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; die and punch treated as discrete rigid bodies, workpiece as a deformable body; mesh size 0.6 mm (mesh-sensitivity analysis); 41,382 C3D8R hexahedral elements (8-node) with reduced integration and hourglass control; punch controlled displacement of 10 mm in the Y (height) direction while the die is fixed; workpiece free to move in X (flow) direction, constrained in Z by the die wall; friction coefficient 0.15 between workpiece and rigid bodies; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping deformation fields from previous passes.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulated dislocation density, grain size and yield strength compared with experimental values at MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 (and initial MAF-0 state); model agrees well up to ~3 passes but underestimates yield strength at 5 passes; simulated yield strength depends on depth from the surface (maximum at centre).

analytical_models.model_note: Grain-size-strengthening constant k calculated as 2374 MPa·μm^0.5 (for a grain-size range 50–13 μm).
α = 0.24, M = 3.0, G = 61 GPa; Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm for the FCC austenite.
Empirical relation (Eq. 7) fitted to dislocation density vs equivalent strain; for this study k1 = 7.9 × 10^15 m^-2 and k2 = 1.813.
Eq. 8 fitted to imposed equivalent strain and grain size; k3 = 0.639. For MAF-0, ε = 0 gives d_f = d_0 = 50 μm.

unmapped_findings: MAF-0 (solutionized and water-quenched, 0 MAF pass) is the reference/baseline state against which the strengthening contributions of the forged states are measured; all dislocation- and grain-refinement strengthening increments are quoted relative to MAF-0 (0 Pass shows '-' for both contributions).

For the MAF-0 (0 pass) condition, all strengthening parameters are already included in σ_0 (380 MPa); grain-boundary and dislocation strengthening only become explicit contributions in subsequent MAF passes.
The alloy possesses very high ductility (greater than 70% at room temperature and greater than 95% at 300 °C) as well as high formability, motivating its use in the MAF study.
MAF-0 is the initial annealed/solutionized state with the (111) peak most intense in XRD (before texturing changes to (220)); the sample is strongly textured before MAF.
The material could only be forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt; MAF-0 corresponds to the initial annealed state before any forging pass (equivalent strain 0).
